changes.before: Recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity moderated in the first half of the year.
changes.after: Available indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.

changes.before: judges that downside risks to employment have risen.
changes.after: judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months.

changes.before: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4 to 4‑1/4 percent.
changes.after: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.

changes.before: The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage‑backed securities.
changes.after: The Committee decided to conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings on December 1.

parsed.rationale: The Committee cut again and announced an end to balance-sheet runoff on December 1, both easing steps, though a hawkish dissent and a firmer description of activity partly offset the dovish signal. Forward guidance was unchanged, so the net shift is modestly dovish.

spans.quote: Recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity moderated in the first half of the year.
judges that downside risks to employment have risen.
the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4 to 4‑1/4 percent.
The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage‑backed securities.
Voting against this action was Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point at this meeting.
Available indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months.
the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
The Committee decided to conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings on December 1.

Voting against this action were Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point at this meeting, and Jeffrey R. Schmid, who preferred no change to the target range for the federal funds rate at this meeting.
